quiz.title: Approximations by Differentials Quiz (Ex 6.4)
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the Exercise 6.4 method: using dy = f'(x) dx to approximate roots, powers and small changes. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Application of Derivatives Exercise 6.4 — approximations

questions.q: Using differentials, the approximate value of √25.3 is:
questions.explanation: Let f(x) = √x, x = 25, Δx = 0.3. f'(x) = 1/(2√x) = 1/10, so dy = 0.1 × 0.3 = 0.03. Hence √25.3 ≈ 5 + 0.03 = 5.03.

questions.q: In the approximation method of Exercise 6.4, the differential dy equals:
questions.explanation: By definition dy = f'(x) dx, and for a small change Δx we take Δy ≈ dy, so f(x + Δx) ≈ f(x) + f'(x) Δx.

questions.q: The approximate value of (26)^(1/3) using differentials is:
If there is an error of 2% in measuring the edge of a cube, the approximate percentage error in its volume is:
questions.explanation: V = x^3, so dV/V = 3(dx/x). A 2% error in the edge gives 3 × 2% = 6% error in volume.

questions.q: Using differentials, the approximate value of (255)^(1/4) is:
The radius of a sphere increases from 9 cm to 9.05 cm. The approximate increase in surface area (S = 4πr²) is:
The edge of a cube is 10 cm and increases by 0.1 cm. The approximate increase in its volume is:
questions.explanation: V = x^3, so dV = 3x² dx = 3(10)²(0.1) = 30 cm³.

questions.q: For a small change Δx, the value f(x + Δx) is approximated as:
questions.explanation: The linear approximation is f(x + Δx) ≈ f(x) + f'(x)Δx, which is the basis of every Exercise 6.4 estimate.

faq.q: What does Exercise 6.4 of Application of Derivatives cover?
faq.a: It covers approximations using differentials — estimating values like square roots, cube roots and small powers, and finding approximate errors in area or volume, all from the formula dy = f'(x) dx.

faq.q: What is the main formula used in these approximation problems?
faq.a: The linear approximation f(x + Δx) ≈ f(x) + f'(x) Δx. You pick a nearby value x where f(x) is exact, then add the differential dy = f'(x) Δx to correct it.

faq.q: How do you approximate √25.3 by differentials?
faq.a: Take f(x) = √x with x = 25 and Δx = 0.3. Since f'(x) = 1/(2√x) = 0.1, the change is dy = 0.03, so √25.3 ≈ 5.03.

faq.q: How is percentage error in volume related to error in the edge?
faq.a: For a cube, V = x³ gives dV/V = 3(dx/x), so the percentage error in volume is three times the percentage error in the edge. A 2% edge error means about 6% in volume.
